=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:408-413 (issue_family_marker), 136 (_ISSUE_EXAMPLE_RE) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: issue_family_marker uses _ISSUE_EXAMPLE_RE with re.S (non-greedy .*?) to remove the first fenced example block before scanning for family markers. A logged command containing four backticks on its own line terminates the example match early, leaving the rest of the body (including the real family marker) outside the removed portion. The function trusts the last family marker in the remaining text.
  WHY: A legacy permission-prompt issue containing such a command — for instance, a shell command echoing a four-backtick fence — would be assigned the forged family by index_issues. Later prompts in that family would be commented on the wrong issue instead of filed for their actual family.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:279-303 (_family_segments), especially line 292 (token == "<<") | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The heredoc detection check token == "<<" in _family_segments can never be True. _shell_tokens creates a shlex tokenizer with punctuation_chars=_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS = ";&|\n<>()" (line 117-219). With < and > in the punctuation charset, shlex produces two separate < tokens for every << in the input. The token "<<" is never emitted. The heredoc construct is therefore never added to any command_family result.
  WHY: Heredoc variants and non-heredoc variants of the same command share one family instead of being classified into separate families. For example, python3 - <<'EOF'\n...\nEOF and python3 -m pytest -q would both land in the same python3 family without the heredoc construct to distinguish them, causing the wrong issue to receive family comments.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:352-360 (_family_word), 179-214 (_segment_shape), especially the subcommand detection at lines 207-211 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: _family_word calls _segment_shape to extract a subcommand, but _segment_shape detects the subcommand only on the first positional argument (positionals == 1 at line 210). When a command carries a global option that takes a value before the subcommand — such as gh -R owner/repo api ... — the option's value consumes positionals == 1 as a non-subcommand *, and the real subcommand api arrives at positionals == 2, where the gh api special case at line 208 requires shape[1] == "api" to fire. Since -R occupies shape[1], that check fails. The token is dropped. _family_word then returns just gh instead of gh api.
  WHY: A new prompt for gh -R owner/repo api ... and one for gh -R owner/repo issue view ... both get family word gh and are routed to the same family issue, despite the family key being designed to keep subcommands apart.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:697-727 (file_patterns), specifically the gap between reading the family index at line 698-701 and creating the issue at line 718-724. | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Family index lookup and issue creation are separate operations with no reservation or recheck. The index is read once at line 698 and the decision (family_home) is computed once at line 705. If two concurrent file_patterns invocations each read an empty family entry for a given family, both proceed to create new issues on lines 718-724.
  WHY: Concurrent stage sessions in different implementation runs could each file a new family issue for different signatures in the same family, producing a duplicate issue. The likelihood is low — stage sessions for one implementation are serial, and the window between index read and issue POST is narrow — but the code has no guard against it.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: issue_family_marker, lines 408-413; _occurrence_block, lines 520-522 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The family-marker parser removes only the example block it recognizes, but the example is inserted without escaping inside a four-backtick fence. A recorded command containing a closing fence followed by a valid family marker makes that marker appear outside the parsed example. On a legacy issue without its own family marker, index_issues then accepts the injected marker.
  WHY: A crafted permission-prompt command can make a legacy issue appear to belong to an unrelated family. Later reports for that family are commented on the wrong issue instead of being filed or routed to their actual family.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _family_word, lines 352-360; _segment_shape, lines 179-214 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: _family_word depends on _segment_shape to retain subcommands. When a global option with a value precedes the subcommand, _segment_shape treats the option value as the first positional argument and drops the subcommand. For example, both `gh -R owner/repo api ...` and `gh -R owner/repo issue view ...` reduce to the family word `gh`.
  WHY: Different GitHub CLI operations are assigned the same family, so a new shape for one operation is commented on the other operation’s family issue rather than opening or selecting its own.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: file_patterns, lines 697-727 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The family index is read once before filing, and creating an issue does not reserve the family or recheck the index. Separate stage sessions can therefore both observe no issue for a family and each create an issue for a different signature in that family.
  WHY: The issue-pickup flow starts a session per target issue, and each stage files its permission-prompt report. If two such reports for the same family overlap, both POST new issues; the in-run family registration only coordinates patterns within each individual invocation, so duplicate family issues remain.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: `_family_segments` around line 292, specifically `heredoc = heredoc or token == "<<"` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The heredoc detection check `token == "<<"` can never match because the shlex tokenizer with `punctuation_chars=_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS` (where `_SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS = ";&|\n<>()"`) produces individual `<` tokens, not a combined `<<` token.
  WHY: Commands containing heredocs do not get the `heredoc` construct in their `command_family` return value. Heredoc and non-heredoc variants of the same command share one family instead of being classified into separate families. However, the test `test_command_family` expects `("python3", ("heredoc",))` for `"python3 - <<'EOF'\nprint(1)\nEOF"`, which would fail if this bug exists. The PR description claims 93 tests passed, so either the test is actually failing, or there is a subtlety in shlex tokenization that combines consecutive `<` characters into a single `<<` token despite `punctuation_chars`. This needs verification.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: `_family_word` around line 352-360, relying on `_segment_shape` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_family_word` relies on `_segment_shape` to find a subcommand, but `_segment_shape` only keeps the subcommand at `positionals == 1`. When a command has global options with values before the subcommand (e.g., `gh -R owner/repo api`), the subcommand `api` is at `positionals == 2` or later, so it is not kept in the shape. Both `gh -R owner/repo api` and `gh -R owner/repo issue view` would get the family word `gh` instead of `gh api` and `gh issue`.
  WHY: Prompts for different subcommands of the same tool, when preceded by global options, are merged into one family. A new prompt for one subcommand can be commented on the existing family issue for another subcommand, merging distinct causes.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: `file_patterns` around lines 695-727 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Family lookup and issue creation are separate operations with no reservation or recheck. Concurrent `file_patterns` invocations (from concurrent stage sessions) can each read an empty family index, then each create an issue for a different signature in the same family.
  WHY: Concurrent stage reports can produce duplicate family issues instead of converging on one issue. However, this is the same race that already exists for signature-based filing today, and the family feature does not make it worse. Sessions are typically sequential, so concurrent invocations are rare. The impact is duplicate issues that operators can close as duplicates.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: `issue_family_marker` around lines 408-413; the example is interpolated into a four-backtick fence at lines 520-522 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `issue_family_marker` removes only the first fenced example block before trusting the last family marker. The command is inserted into that fence without escaping, so a multiline command containing a closing four-backtick line and a family marker leaves that marker outside the block the parser removes.
  WHY: A legacy permission-prompt issue containing such a logged command could be assigned the forged family by `index_issues`. Later prompts in that family would be commented on the wrong issue. However, this requires a very specific attack scenario: a legacy issue whose example contains four backticks followed by a family
